title: Basis of the Difference Returned to the Customer on a Northbeam Returns and Restocking Exchange
content:
The difference returned to the customer on an exchange is the price paid on the line, times the units coming back, less the price of the replacement going out, and the whole of that drop, being 100 per cent of it, is returned. The price of the replacement going out is today's shelf price of the stock number going out, which is the unit price on the most recent merchandise line the records carry for that stock number, and where the records carry none it is the price paid on the line itself. Where the price of the replacement going out is the same as or more than the price paid on the line, the drop is nothing rather than a negative figure, and the drop is held at nothing before the share of the drop is taken. The difference returned is never less than nothing and is rounded to the cent. Where the schedule settles an exchange like for like only, no difference is settled at all. The stock number recorded on the exchange is the stock number of the item the return was raised on, since the replacement going out is the same model.

## The quantity, put as a definition

| Element | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| the price paid | the price paid on the returned line, times the units coming back |
| today's shelf price | the unit price on the most recent merchandise line the records of Northbeam Purchase Orders and Fulfilment carry for that stock number; where they carry none, the price paid on the line itself |
| the drop | the price paid, times the units, less the price of the replacement going out |
| the floor on the drop | where the price of the replacement going out is the same as or more than the price paid, the drop is nothing rather than a negative figure, held at nothing before the share of the drop is taken |
| the share returned | 100 per cent of the drop |
| the floor on the difference | the difference returned is never less than nothing |
| the rounding | to the cent |
| the stock number recorded | the stock number of the item the return was raised on, the replacement being the same model |

Holding the difference to nothing at its lowest and rounding it to the cent are taken last of all; the floor on the drop stands earlier, before the share of the drop is taken.

Where the Northbeam Returns and Restocking schedule the line falls under settles an exchange like for like only, no difference is settled at all, whatever the drop would have come to.

## Worked through on hypothetical inputs

*One unit, 900.00 USD paid on the line, the most recent merchandise line for that stock number carrying a unit price of 740.00 USD, on a schedule that settles a difference at today's shelf price.* The price paid times the units is 900.00 USD; the replacement going out is priced at 740.00 USD; the drop is 160.00 USD; the whole of it is returned, so the difference is 160.00 USD.

*Two units at 400.00 USD each, the most recent merchandise line for that stock number carrying 380.00 USD.* The price paid times the units is 800.00 USD, the replacement going out is priced at 380.00 USD, and the difference returned is 420.00 USD.

*One unit, 265.00 USD paid, the most recent merchandise line for that stock number carrying 341.00 USD.* The replacement going out is priced above the price paid, so the drop is nothing rather than a negative figure, and it is held at nothing before the share is taken; the whole of nothing is nothing, and the difference is 0.00 USD.

*One unit, 265.00 USD paid, no merchandise line carried for that stock number at all.* The replacement going out is priced at the price paid on the line, 265.00 USD, so the price of the replacement is the same as the price paid, the drop is nothing, and the difference is 0.00 USD.

*Any line on a schedule that settles an exchange like for like only.* No difference is settled at all, so the difference returned is 0.00 USD.
